stem: Which statement about gastro-oesophageal reflux disease risk in children is correct?

options.text: Obesity is a recognised risk factor for gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
Obesity protects against gastro-oesophageal reflux disease in children
Weight is unrelated to reflux risk once a child is older than 1 year
Only congenital anomalies are listed as reflux risk factors
Reflux symptoms are always normal if vomiting began in infancy

explanation: Obesity is a recognised risk factor for gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. In a child with persistent reflux symptoms, excess weight is therefore clinically relevant.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Obesity is a recognised paediatric risk factor for gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and should be considered when reviewing persistent reflux symptoms.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because obesity is listed as a recognised risk factor for gastro-oesophageal reflux disease.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because obesity is associated with increased, not reduced, reflux risk.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because weight can remain relevant to reflux risk beyond infancy.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because reflux risk factors include obesity and other factors, not only congenital anomalies.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because vomiting in infancy does not automatically mean later reflux symptoms are normal
